source.title: Deep Unlearn: Benchmarking Machine Unlearning for Image Classification
source.authors: Xavier F. Cadet; Anastasia Borovykh; M. Malekzadeh; Sara Ahmadi-Abhari; Hamed Haddadi

page_placements.theme: Unlearned models stay near the original and distinguishable from a retrained model (non-MIA traces)
Membership-inference residue after unlearning (privacy signal, under- or over-unlearning)

record.tranche_reason: Benchmarks unlearning with membership-inference measures that bear on data removal, but does not test whether knowledge can be recovered by the attacks named in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates image-classification unlearning using U-MIA and U-LiRA. These test whether forgotten examples remain distinguishable as training members, not whether their targeted knowledge can be recovered. Rows are therefore linked to none of the listed versions. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting.
record.test_reason: This is a benchmark of 18 approximate unlearning methods for image classifiers (ResNet18 and TinyViT on MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10/100 and UTKFace). It evaluates forget/retain accuracy, membership inference (U-MIA, U-LiRA), run time and L2 weight distance. No recovery attack is run: no relearning fine-tuning, no activation edits, no post-hoc quantization, no prompting. The setting is not LLM knowledge unlearning. WMDP is cited only in related work. The record's 'tests/T2' is wrong: membership detectability is a different construct from recovering suppressed knowledge.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that MSG and CT, tuned properly, perform best and most consistently across datasets, architectures and seeds, and resist both U-MIA and U-LiRA. They add that FT is a reasonable baseline, GA should be replaced by NG+, and approximate unlearning is only as strong as the attacks tested against it.
record.recipe_differences: Benchmarks approximate machine-unlearning procedures for image classifiers, rather than testing LLM unlearning recovery recipes or attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary across model seeds and architecture; the authors also report differences across datasets and models.

fits_no_version.finding: A retrained model that never saw the forget set still has 10% of CIFAR-100 forget images flagged as members across all 10 seeds. Some images are flagged across all seeds by 13 of 18 methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weak population MIA flags some forget examples even for exact retraining, so MIA detectability alone is a noisy unlearning signal.

fits_no_version.finding: MSG and CT are reported to resist the per-sample U-LiRA membership attack on CIFAR-10 ResNet18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In image-classifier unlearning, some approximate methods resist strong per-sample membership inference.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix C / Figure 4: no unlearned ResNet18 gets close to the retrained model's weights, and most stay closer to the original model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Approximate unlearning in image classifiers leaves weights near the original model rather than the retrained one; this is weight-space residue, but recovery is not tested.

record.peer_reviewed: European Symposium on Security and Privacy
record.problems: The membership-inference attacks measure example membership, not recovery of targeted knowledge. U-LiRA numerical values are shown only in a figure and are not stated in the text. The experiments concern randomly selected image-classification examples with a fixed 10% forgetting budget, not LLM knowledge unlearning.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were extracted: most benchmark tables report method-by-dataset performance metrics that do not measure any claim version's recovery behavior. Figure 2 distributions and Figure 3 numerical values are not reported in the text.

untested.parts: No LLM targeted-knowledge unlearning, and no check of whether simple attacks recover forgotten knowledge.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack after unlearning.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of blocked access versus deletion. L2 weight distance is reported, but recovery is not tested.
No post-unlearning low-bit quantization attack. PRMQ's half-precision step is part of that unlearning method.
No prompting, rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery.
MSG and CT are claimed robust only to membership-inference attacks, not to the recovery attacks in versions B–E.

missing.what: L2 distance result: unlearned models stay closer to the original than to the retrained model's weights. It bears on none of the versions directly but is relevant context.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from tests/T2 to cites_only/T6: the study is image-classification unlearning evaluated by membership inference, and it never tests knowledge recovery. The only link to the claim's sources is a related-work citation of WMDP. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Tests image-classification unlearning, not LLM unlearning; does not test whether a recovery attack restores targeted knowledge after performance is near chance while general ability is retained.
No recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocked access versus deletion.
No post-unlearning low-bit quantization recovery test; PRMQ's quantization is part of its unlearning procedure, not a recovery attack.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery tests.
Does not test a method for resisting the recovery attacks in the claim.

rows.subject: Retrained model (CIFAR-100, ResNet18)
rows.operation_detail: U-MIA tested whether forget-set examples were distinguishable from test-set examples across model initializations.
rows.measure: Percentage of forget-set images identified as belonging to the forget set across all 10 model seeds
rows.note: The authors state this also occurs for the retrained reference model, which never saw the forget examples. This is a membership-detection rate, not a knowledge-recovery measure.
rows.check: Retrained-reference control for membership detection on CIFAR-100 ResNet18. It is not a measure of knowledge recovery, so the link to none is correct. Baseline is 'not stated', but the measure is inherently about the reference model itself.

rows.subject: 13 of 18 unlearning methods (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: U-MIA assessed whether forget-set examples were distinguishable from test-set examples across initialization seeds.
rows.measure: Whether any forget-set examples were correctly identified across all 10 initialization seeds
rows.value: Data points in the forget set were correctly identified across all ten initialization seeds by 13 methods out of 18
rows.note: The authors say the methods may identify different images; this does not measure recovery of the images' targeted content.
rows.check: Aggregate count (13 of 18 methods) of hard-to-forget images under the weak U-MIA. This is membership detectability, not recovery; the link to none is correct.

rows.subject: MSG
rows.operation_detail: Applied the per-sample U-LiRA membership inference attack to unlearned models.
rows.uncertainty: The authors report average and standard deviation; numerical values not stated in text
rows.note: The text characterizes MSG as resisting U-LiRA, but the plot's numerical values are not stated in text. Membership inference is not knowledge recovery.
rows.check: U-LiRA membership accuracy for MSG is shown only in Figure 3. It is a privacy-attack resilience result for an image classifier, not resistance to the claim's recovery attacks, so it is not version F.

rows.subject: CT
rows.operation_detail: Applied the per-sample U-LiRA membership inference attack to unlearned models.
rows.uncertainty: The authors report average and standard deviation; numerical values not stated in text
rows.note: The text characterizes CT as resisting U-LiRA, but the plot's numerical values are not stated in text. Membership inference is not knowledge recovery.
rows.check: Same issue as r3, for CT: figure-only U-LiRA resilience in an image classifier, not version F.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: It cites WMDP (Li et al.), an original source, in its related-work section on benchmarks, and tests no version. So cites_only fits.

tranche.reason: Benchmark of 18 approximate unlearning methods on image classifiers (random-sample forgetting, MIA/U-LiRA). It runs no recovery attack and does not test any LLM knowledge-unlearning version, so T6 fits.

source_check.notes: Image-classifier benchmark. The noise-floor result concerns membership detection, not knowledge recovery. The L2-distance result comes with the authors' caveat that distance to Retrained may be an inadequate unlearning metric (Appendix C). Neither result is evidence on the LLM claim versions.

statements.correction: Text: Retrained model (ResNet18, CIFAR-100): 10% of Forget-set images identified as Forget-set members across all 10 model seeds (U-MIA). Some forget images identified across all ten seeds by 13 of 18 methods; which 13 methods may differ per image.
Fig. 4 caption (Appendix C): none of the unlearned ResNet18 models gets close to the Retrained weights; most are closer to the Original.
